entries.clue: Wolves player who roams around aimlessly? (8)

blocks.note: Wolves is the nickname of an English football club from Wolverhampton; the answer is its full name's second word, singular

annotation.surface: A footballer who drifts about the pitch with no idea of his position.
annotation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, so any of its players is a Wanderer.
annotation.definitionFit: A Wolves player plays for the Wanderers, and a wanderer is literally someone who roams aimlessly.

entries.clue: Long nail finally broke (4)

indicatorNotes.finally: takes the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a pin is a small nail

annotation.surface: A long fingernail has just snapped.
annotation.walkthrough: Long is the verb here, as in to long for something, not the adjective the surface pairs with nail.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to yearn for something absent, as a homesick exile does.

entries.clue: Person from institution’s given home with couple (6)

annotation.surface: Someone released from an institution is sent home along with a pair of companions.
annotation.walkthrough: Couple is a verb here: animals that couple mate.
annotation.definitionFit: An inmate is someone held in a prison or asylum.

entries.clue: Church programme includes top lay musician (7)

indicatorNotes.includes: CE + LIST holds the next letter inside it
indicatorNotes.top: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter

blocks.note: a list of items, as a programme is

annotation.surface: A church's order of service features a leading lay musician.
annotation.walkthrough: Lay here means not ordained, one of the congregation rather than clergy; only its first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A cellist is a musician who plays the cello.

entries.clue: Designer has last of mini skirts in Twiggy’s size (8)

indicatorNotes.last of: the last of a word is its final letter, so the last of mini is its closing I
indicatorNotes.skirts: the edges of a word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: Mary Quant, the designer who popularised the miniskirt

annotation.surface: Mary Quant's miniskirts come in the size the 1960s model Twiggy wore.
annotation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was the 1960s London fashion designer behind the miniskirt, and Twiggy was the model of the same era; skirts looks like clothing but is the verb for edging a word.
annotation.definitionFit: Size and quantity both mean amount or magnitude.

entries.clue: Essentially policed crime surrounding alcohol shop (3-7)

indicatorNotes.Essentially: the essence of a word is its middle
indicatorNotes.surrounding: OFFENCE goes around the other letters

annotation.surface: A crime near a liquor store gets only token attention from the police.
annotation.walkthrough: An off-licence is the British name for a shop selling alcohol to take away, like a liquor store.
annotation.definitionFit: An off-licence is licensed to sell alcohol for drinking off the premises.

entries.clue: Stalls in Kitzbuhel initially keeping old among new skis (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the word's opening letter is used
indicatorNotes.keeping: the rearranged SKIS holds O inside
indicatorNotes.new: the letters of skis are made new, rearranged

annotation.surface: Stalls in an Austrian ski resort stock old gear among the new skis.
annotation.walkthrough: Kitzbuhel is an Austrian ski resort; the O goes after the I of the rearranged skis.
annotation.definitionFit: Kiosks are small stalls selling newspapers, snacks and the like.

entries.clue: Artist, leader of innovation in movement and light (8)

indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, here the I of innovation
indicatorNotes.in: in places one thing inside another, so the I sits within DANCE

annotation.surface: An artist who pioneered new work in dance and lighting.
annotation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the standard crossword artist.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the glow given off by the sun or a lamp, and the surface hides it by making light sound like stage lighting.

entries.clue: Aunt losing housing, just not right (6)

indicatorNotes.losing housing: the outside of AUNT, its first and last letters, is dropped

blocks.note: AUNT without its outer A and T

annotation.surface: An aunt is evicted and it seems simply wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Just wants to be read as merely; here it is the adjective meaning fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Right here is the moral sense, just or proper, and its negation is a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Unemployed setter had clues every now and then (4)

indicatorNotes.every now and then: something done every now and then happens at intervals, so the letters are taken at regular gaps: second, fourth

blocks.note: the setter is I, so the setter had = I'd

annotation.surface: An out-of-work crossword setter only produced clues occasionally.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter is the writer of the puzzle, so it stands for I; I had shortens to I'd.
annotation.definitionFit: Idle means out of work, not employed.

entries.clue: Finally corrected all tags on toys with 75% off (2,4,4)

indicatorNotes.corrected: the letters are put right, rearranged
indicatorNotes.with 75% off: three of the four letters of toys go, leaving the first

blocks.note: TOYS losing three quarters of its letters

annotation.surface: A shop has at last fixed the price tags on its toys, which are now 75% off.
annotation.walkthrough: Finally looks like it tells you to take a last letter, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom matching the adverb: said with relief when something long awaited finally happens.

entries.clue: Look online for live coverage of disputes (6)

indicatorNotes.coverage of: BE covers ROWS, wrapped round it

annotation.surface: Searching the internet for live news reports of disputes.
annotation.walkthrough: Live coverage suggests a broadcast; here BE covers ROWS. Rows, rhyming with cows, is British for arguments.
annotation.definitionFit: The computing sense of an older word for grazing or leafing through books, now used for surfing the web.

entries.clue: Big draw in twitching day’s curlew, maybe (6,4)

indicatorNotes.twitching: twitching means jerking restlessly, so the letters cannot keep still in their order

blocks.note: D = day, the abbreviation used in dates and diaries

annotation.surface: A curlew was the big attraction on a birdwatching day.
annotation.walkthrough: Twitching is British slang for keen birdwatching, which makes the surface fit the answer; here it jumbles the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The curlew is a long-billed bird that wades in mud, one example of a wading bird.

entries.clue: Lawyer’s bag? (8)

blocks.note: the surface suggests a briefcase; a lawyer's actual business is a suit or a case in court
the question mark lets bag be an ordinary piece of luggage

annotation.surface: A briefcase belonging to a lawyer.
annotation.walkthrough: Suit and case both mean a lawsuit, so a lawyer's business is a suit-case; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: The luggage is literally a bag, and the pun splits it into two legal words for a lawsuit.

entries.clue: Even with exam mark reduced by university, a first in Linguistics (7)

indicatorNotes.a first in: the first in a word is its opening letter, borrowing the university grade the surface is about

annotation.surface: A student still got a first in Linguistics despite a marked-down exam.
annotation.walkthrough: A first is a top British degree grade, which the surface uses; the clue wants the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A gradual slope or rise is an even one, without sudden steps.

entries.clue: Working in Canada, startled to see huge snake (8)

indicatorNotes.in: working in Canada puts ON inside the letters of Canada
indicatorNotes.startled: the letters of Canada jump about

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: Someone working in Canada is shocked to come across an enormous snake.
annotation.walkthrough: There are no anacondas in Canada, which is the joke of the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a very large South American snake.

entries.clue: Decay in waste producing toxin (7)

indicatorNotes.waste: the letters are laid waste, broken up

annotation.surface: Rotting rubbish gives off a poison.
annotation.walkthrough: Waste reads as rubbish in the surface; here it is a verb, to wreck.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the classic fast-acting poison of detective fiction.

entries.clue: Detective’s men reportedly under cover (8)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down entry, GUISE comes below DI'S

annotation.surface: A detective's officers are working undercover.
annotation.walkthrough: Under cover suggests one phrase; under places the men below the detective, and cover alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A disguise covers who you really are.

entries.clue: Fence in space nearby (7)

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of space

annotation.surface: Put a fence up in the space next door.
annotation.walkthrough: In belongs to the definition, not to a container.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the phrasal verb: surrounding a field with a barrier so nothing gets out.

entries.clue: Insist head coach’s right leaving (8)

indicatorNotes.leaving: right leaving means the R departs from the word, so TRAIN drops it

annotation.surface: Insisting that the head coach should be allowed to quit.
annotation.walkthrough: Coach is the verb to train, not a sports manager.
annotation.definitionFit: The sense of asserting firmly, as when someone maintains their innocence, rather than keeping something in repair.

entries.clue: Online image for travel centre’s American sailor (6)

indicatorNotes.centre’s: the centre of a word is its middle, and with six letters that is the two in the middle

annotation.surface: A travel hub's website shows a picture of a US sailor.
annotation.walkthrough: A tar, or jack tar, is an old word for a sailor.
annotation.definitionFit: A computing sense of a Hindu word for a god's earthly form: the picture standing in for you on a website.

entries.clue: Special care, ewes we lost returning to fold (6)

indicatorNotes.Special: the letters of care are made special, rearranged
indicatorNotes.lost: ewes that have lost we no longer have those two letters, leaving ES
indicatorNotes.returning: the remaining ES goes back to front

blocks.note: EWES minus WE is ES, turned round

annotation.surface: Special care is needed as some ewes went missing coming back to the sheepfold.
annotation.walkthrough: Fold looks like a sheep pen, fitting the ewes; it is the crease in paper or cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: The fold here is the line pressed into paper or cloth, not the sheep pen the ewes suggest; the noun sense is a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Scout out money for business (6)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters are out of place

annotation.surface: Scouting around for cash to fund a company.
annotation.walkthrough: Scout out reads as one phrasal verb; out is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Custom is the trade a shop gets from its customers, its business.

entries.clue: Graduate doctor weeps, admitting student cheats (10)

indicatorNotes.admitting: admitting means letting in, as a door admits a visitor, so OOZES takes L inside

annotation.surface: A newly qualified doctor breaks down on learning a student cheated.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheats is the verb here, not a noun for dishonest people.
annotation.definitionFit: To bamboozle someone is to trick or cheat them.

entries.clue: College vote retains sport as essential principle (4)

indicatorNotes.retains: C and X hold RU between them

blocks.note: a cross on a ballot paper

annotation.surface: A college ballot keeps sport at the heart of its values.
annotation.walkthrough: Rugby union is a popular British sport, abbreviated RU.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin for cross, now used for the heart of a problem or argument; a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Pass time with young horse (4)

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass

annotation.surface: Spending time with a young horse.
annotation.walkthrough: Pass time reads as one idea, killing time; pass is the mountain gap.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, loosely: strictly it is a male under four, and the clue's broader phrase covers it.

entries.clue: Shook container with wine (6)

annotation.surface: Someone shook a bottle of wine.
annotation.walkthrough: Container looks like a container instruction; it is simply a JAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense, of a sudden jolt that rattles something or someone.

entries.clue: See fewer without sin (8)

annotation.surface: Seeing fewer people once you give up sinning.
annotation.walkthrough: See wants to be a church see or a noun; here it is the verb, to notice.
annotation.definitionFit: A spotless character is morally unblemished, without sin.
